changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/8318-jsdoc-default-tag-corrections.md`

- names `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` — edited by this change

  > - `CRUDDialogSchema.size` / `.closeOnOutsideClick` / `.closeOnEscape` / `.showClose` — there is no `register('crud-dialog'` anywhere, so no node of that type ever reaches a renderer. Recorded once on the interface. Per key, the name census differs: two spellings occur nowhere outside the declaration and its zod twin, and `showClose`'s one other occurrence (`renderers/overlay/drawer.tsx:38`) belongs to `DrawerSchema`. - `ActionSchema.level` — `type: 'action'` is not a rendered node type, and `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`, which is what makes `method` / `chainMode` / `reload` / `close` live, does not read `level`. - `CardSchema.variant` — `card` IS registered, twice, and neither registration reads it: the `ui` route forwards the key to `ui/card.tsx`, which spreads onto a `div` and mentions `variant` nowhere, and the `page` route forwards only its designer props. - `PageNodeSchema.isDefault` — `page` IS registered, and `PageRenderer` neither reads the key nor forwards it: the wrapper element gets `toDomProps(props)`, an allow-list that does not carry it.

### `.changeset/action-keys-warning-text-5642.md`

- names `ActionRunner.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` — edited by this change

  > Both halves of the message's tail had outlived the change they described. It told the author the key was warned about rather than rejected because `ActionDef` "still carries `[key: string]: any`" — objectstack#4075 step 3 deleted that index signature, and `actionKeys.pin.test.ts` pins the deletion in the opposite direction (`{ ActionDef: false, ActionContext: true }`), while `actionDef-closed-surface.test.ts` pins that `tsc` now rejects exactly such a key at the construction site. And it prescribed promoting the key to an explicit field on `ActionDef` "(packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts)" — that file holds the INVENTORY (`ACTION_DEF_KEYS`); the interface is in `ActionRunner.ts`. The wrong pointer had teeth: an author who followed it edited the inventory alone, which is precisely the half-change the pin test reddens on, since it re-derives the inventory from the interface's AST.

### `.changeset/host-dispatch-action-keys-5611.md`

- names `actions/actionKeys.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts` — edited by this change

  > Adds an exported `HOST_DISPATCH_ACTION_KEYS` (sole member `overrideNotice`) to `actions/actionKeys.ts` and unions it into `KNOWN_ACTION_KEYS`, which is the fourth input to that set and the first one that is not an authored-surface mirror. Measured before and after on the exact dispatch the bar composes: the warning went from one call naming `overrideNotice` to none, `KNOWN_ACTION_KEYS` grew by exactly one member, and an action carrying a real typo alongside it still warns — naming `targt` only.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `1b30c0fe0` (merge-base with origin/main): 4 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1855 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2467 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36790692480)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b70c10a4d1c483e80d45020cbf774bfcd3d83818`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #10929 (body, triage `5868003195`, unlock `5904384435`, claim `5920190491`, os-dev-report `5921249112`), PR #11282 (body, 5 files, diff against `main`; the head's parent is `18d1a0abd`, the tip the claim read), and the 43 check-runs on the head (`filter=latest`; 42 at my first read, the `Test` rollup joined once its shards finished). Context reads at the head by `contents?ref=`: `packages/core/package.json`, `packages/core/src/index.ts`, the actions barrel, `actionKeys.ts`, `ActionRunner.ts`, `ActionDefaultInspector.tsx`, the two `actionKeys` pin tests, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-changeset-claims.mjs`, `changeset-guard.yml`, AGENTS.md, and 28 action-surface files across `components`, `app-shell`, `react`, `plugin-detail`, `plugin-grid`, `core` and `scripts`. Upstream context read at the 17.5.0 spec tag commit `0f6dcac5e9`: `metadata-protocol/src/unauthorable-nodes.ts` and the served-schema derivation in `protocol.ts`.

**Gate verdicts on the head.** 43 check-runs, all completed (12 were still in progress when I started; waited 490 s in the foreground): 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` (the two coverage jobs and `dependabot`), 0 failed. The ones this diff answers to: `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Test` and its eight shards, `Test (dist pins)`, `Build & E2E`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Inert vi.mock Specifier Check`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` — all `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ActionDef` loses `aria` — right.** The member was `aria?: SpecActionInput['aria']`, which at spec 17.5.0 resolves to `undefined` (the tombstone's input type is `never`, optional). Removing it narrows the TYPE-level accept set of a fresh literal by `{ aria: undefined }` (the dev's reverse check: TS2353 now, clean before) and makes a `.aria` read TS2339; the runtime accept set does not move, because nothing validates an `ActionDef` at runtime and structural assignment of a non-literal is untouched. `ActionDef` has no index signature (the pin test's `hasIndexSignature` guard, and none in the interface at the head), so every in-repo reader of `.aria` would have failed CI `Type Check`; it is green. The card's own measurement at `f8a9d0fb05` was 0 readers; I found 0 in the 28 action-surface files read at the head (`record-quick-actions.tsx` reads `schema.aria` of the PLACING node, which the card names as the correct home, not an action's).
2. **`ACTION_DEF_KEYS` loses `'aria'` — right, and every reader named.** Readers at the head: (i) `KNOWN_ACTION_KEYS` = `ACTION_DEF_KEYS` ∪ `SPEC_ACTION_KEYS` ∪ `NAVIGATION_ALIAS_KEYS` ∪ `HOST_DISPATCH_ACTION_KEYS` minus `RETIRED_ACTION_KEYS`; `aria` stays in `SPEC_ACTION_KEYS` (the spec mirror the pin test asserts against `ActionSchema.shape`, which still carries the tombstone) and `RETIRED_ACTION_KEYS` holds only `execute`, so `KNOWN_ACTION_KEYS`, `classifyActionKeys` and `warnOnUnknownActionKeys` are behaviour-identical: a stored `aria` warns neither before nor after, exactly like `bulkEnabled` and `shortcut` today. (ii) `actionKeys.pin.test.ts` re-derives the list from the `ActionDef` AST, so the two edits had to move together and did. (iii) The `warnOnUnknownActionKeys` prescription names `ACTION_DEF_KEYS` as text only. No reader outside `packages/core/src/actions` in the files read; `check-action-forward-parity.mjs` does not read it. The repo-wide closure is the eight `Test` shards and `Type Check` on the head.
3. **`actionKeys.types.test.ts` row re-pointed — right.** `{ aria: { ariaLabel: 'Approve' } }` was VALID before 17.5.0, so it is the discriminating row: rejected against `ActionDef`, clean against the `IndexSignatureOnly` control, by the harness that compiles both.
4. **Branch 1 of the ruling honoured — right.** `ActionDefaultInspector.tsx` is not in the file list; `RETIRED_FIELDS` at the head is still `['bulkEnabled', 'shortcut']`; no `aria` row was added. That is the triage dispatch shape (`5868003195`, item 1) and the claim's own conditional.
5. **The measurement behind branch 1 — the fixture is derived, not hand-built, and reproduces the strip rather than importing it.** The served 17.5.0 payload (44 properties; `aria`, `bulkEnabled`, `shortcut` absent) and the 44 = 44 top-level key match were measured in a throwaway probe against the published `metadata-protocol@17.5.0` `getMetaTypes()`; that measurement is REPORTED, not in the tree, and I could not re-run it read-only. What is in the tree: `getMetadataTypeSchema('action')` from the installed `@objectstack/spec/kernel`, `z.toJSONSchema` with `unrepresentable: 'any'` and `io: 'input'`, then a top-level filter dropping a non-required `{ not: {} }` property. Read against the upstream at `0f6dcac5e9`: `acceptsNothing` and the property filter in `unauthorable-nodes.ts` are the same predicate; the served derivation `toJsonSchemaSafe` takes the `io: 'input'` retry arm when the output derivation is a husk, and additionally passes `override: markErasedAuthoringInput` (annotates erased `ZodPipe` arms, adds or removes no top-level property, consistent with the 44 = 44) and walks nested schemas (irrelevant to a pin that reads one top-level key). So the reproduction is faithful for what the pin reads. **Durability:** the spec half tracks the installed pin (a later spec that drops or reshapes the tombstone flows through `getMetadataTypeSchema`); the strip half is frozen in the test, so an upstream `metadata-protocol` that STOPS stripping would put `aria` back in the served payload while this pin stays green. Ablation leg B shows that sensitivity exactly: skip the strip and both cases fail on `#mdf-aria`. That is the accepted cost of objectui not installing `metadata-protocol`, and the fixture header says so. The pin is right for what it pins: the inspector adds no `aria` control of its own, and `SchemaForm` builds rows from the schema's properties, never from keys only the draft carries.
6. **Stored-`aria` pin — right.** An action storing `aria: { ariaLabel, role }` mounts without throwing; the Label control reads `Approve`; the More-fields host renders (the served `order` row is found); nothing named aria is offered. Nothing is stripped client-side: `onPatch` is inert in the test, the inspector reads `draft` only for curated keys, and the block stays in the draft. What it shows is the action as usual, with the block invisible and not removable from this editor (see ③, note 3).
7. **Ablation legs — right, as reported.** Leg A (an `ARIA label` curated control planted in the inspector, marker 1): over the 12 files referencing the inspector, `1 failed | 11 passed`, `2 failed | 116 passed`, the 2 being exactly the two new pins. Leg B (served strip skipped in the fixture): `2 failed (2)`, both on `#mdf-aria`. Both from committed HEAD through `ablation-replace.mjs`, restore proven. The two legs cover the two ways the inspector could offer the key (a control of its own; a More-fields row), which is what the detector `offered()` looks for. Not re-run here.
8. **Changeset — one, `@object-ui/core: patch`.** Level judged in ②.

### ② Semver level

- **`ActionDef` is public.** `packages/core/package.json` exports only `.` to `dist/index.d.ts`; `src/index.ts` carries `export * from './actions/index.js'`, and that barrel carries `export * from './ActionRunner.js'` and `export * from './actionKeys.js'`. So both `ActionDef` and `ACTION_DEF_KEYS` sit on `@object-ui/core`'s root surface.
- **The built diff narrows that surface.** A published interface loses a declared member and a published constant loses an element (its `as const` union and its runtime contents). Nothing widens. The value `no` in the claim (`5920190491`) and in the PR body is true; the ARM is missing. Under the fleet's own reading of the declaration (`clause2-line.mjs`: a diff that narrows a published accept set answers `no` and is breaking), the line must read `no (narrowing)`. No objectui gate reads the arm today (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads frontmatter levels only; `check-changeset-claims.mjs` reads bodies against touched files; neither mentions the clause), so the four green changeset checks do not decide this.
- **The level must be `minor`, not `patch`.** AGENTS.md §版本号策略 and the header of `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: `major` is refused (the 39-package fixed group is pinned to the `@objectstack` major), and objectui's OWN breaking changes ship as `minor` with the break spelled out in the changeset body. The body already describes the compile-level change (the error moves from a type mismatch against `undefined` to an excess-property error) and names the removed `ACTION_DEF_KEYS` entry, but its sentence "Any value was already refused" is not exact: explicit `aria: undefined` compiled, a `.aria` read compiled, and `'aria'` satisfied `keyof ActionDef` and `typeof ACTION_DEF_KEYS[number]`; those stop compiling. The reach is narrow (the card measured 0 in-repo readers; `Type Check` confirms 0 at the head), which is why this is a `minor` and not a hold.
- **Correction for the seat before landing, not a FAIL:** the declaration line on the PR body takes the arm `no (narrowing)`; the changeset frontmatter goes to `minor` and its body names the removed member and the removed inventory entry as the break. The code diff is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none. Deviations, each judged:

1. **Container restart, tier-B closure re-run in two halves.** Process only; nothing pushed was redone; `Type Check` and `Build & E2E` on the head are the closure. Accepted.
